name: Hoist Finance AB
reason: Non-performing consumer-debt purchaser whose returns are set by credit cycles and NPL portfolio pricing: EPS went from SEK 6.45 (2019) to -0.53 and -2.33 (2020-21) before a 10y-high SEK 11.75 in 2025 with EBIT margin at the 100th pctile, 10y avg ROE 10.1% and net debt/EBITDA 6.9x; cyclical with no specialness.

name: Bankinter SA
reason: Best-run Spanish bank (10y avg ROE 12.1%, EPS EUR 0.31 to 0.43 over 2015-19 even at negative rates), but 2025 EPS of EUR 1.18 is 2.7x the 2021 level on the Euribor/NIM tailwind and at its 10y high, so the normalised through-cycle earnings base cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: KBC Group N.V.
reason: Strong Belgian/CEE bancassurance franchise (10y avg ROE 13.4%) but EPS was flat at EUR 5.33-5.83 through the zero-rate years 2016-21 and the rise to a 10y-high EUR 8.70 (2025) is NIM-driven; 10y EPS CAGR only 4.8% leaves the >=7% route rate-dependent.

name: Hera S.p.A.
reason: Municipally controlled Italian multi-utility (waste, water, gas/power supply) with consensus EPS growth of -0.2%/+5.0%/+4.5% for FY1-FY3, 10y avg ROIC 5.2%, net debt/EBITDA 3.2x and acquisitions at 0.29x FCF; regulated/commodity-exposed returns with no >=7% route.

name: UNITE Group plc
reason: UK student-accommodation REIT: FFO/share flat at GBP 0.44-0.46 over 2023-25 while the share count grew 7.7%/yr, consensus FY1 -13.1% and LTG -3.2%, net debt/EBITDA 7.9x and acquisitions at 0.69x FCF (Empiric); no per-share growth route.

name: Umicore SA
reason: Catalysts, battery materials and precious-metals recycling: EPS EUR 2.77 (2021) collapsed to 1.06 (2024) and 1.20 (2025) on the battery-cathode write-downs and PGM prices, 10y EPS CAGR 1.0%, 10y avg ROIC 5.3%; commodity- and technology-exposed with no forecastable growth.

name: Munchener Ruckversicherungs-Gesellschaft AG
reason: Premier global reinsurer with EPS EUR 18.86 (2015) to 47.04 (2025) and shares -2.4%/yr, but EPS is at its 10y high after the 2023-25 hard P&C market, consensus FY2 is -2.4% and cat/natural-catastrophe losses (2017 EPS EUR 2.44, 2020 -54.5%) make 5-10 year earnings hard to forecast; matches TRV/WRB/KNSL precedent.

name: Danske Bank A/S
reason: Nordic bank with 10y avg ROE 9.0% and EPS that fell from DKK 22.2 (2017) to 4.7 (2020) after the Estonian money-laundering scandal; the 2025 EPS of DKK 27.9 is a NIM-driven 10y high, 10y revenue CAGR only 1.5%, and consensus FY2/FY3 +9.5%/+6.6%; not best-in-class through the cycle.

name: Komercni banka a.s.
reason: Societe Generale-controlled Czech bank with EPS flat at CZK 79.0 over 2017-19 and CZK 95.6 in 2025 only modestly above 2022's 93.0, 10y EPS CAGR 3.5%, consensus FY1 -4.2% and FY2/FY3 +5.8% (LTG 2.5%); rate-driven with no >=7% route.

name: Banque Cantonale de Geneve SA
reason: Canton-of-Geneva-controlled bank whose EPS grew from CHF 1.11 (2016) to 3.09 (2025), but 10y avg ROE is only 7.8% and consensus is -1.0%/+4.2%/+1.0% for FY1-FY3 as Swiss rates return to zero; ordinary returns with no growth route.

name: BAWAG Group AG
reason: Highly efficient Austrian bank (10y avg ROE 13.0%, EPS EUR 3.01 in 2017 to 3.97 in 2021 at zero rates, then 10.87 in 2025), but the 2025 EPS is a NIM-driven 10y high and the consensus FY2 jump of +27% leans on acquisitions (Knab, Barclays Consumer Bank Europe, Peak Bancorp US), so growth is partly deal- and rate-dependent.

name: ABN AMRO Bank N.V.
reason: Dutch state-controlled (NLFI) bank with EPS of EUR 2.45 in 2025 below the 2017 peak of 2.89, 10y EPS CAGR 1.9%, flat revenue (0.3%/yr) and 10y avg ROE 9.1%; consensus +32.8% FY1 rests on the NIBC deal and cost cuts, not a durable franchise.

name: Talanx AG
reason: HDI-mutual-controlled insurer/reinsurer (Hannover Re) with EPS EUR 3.00 to 9.60 (12.3% 10y CAGR, 10y avg ROE 12.0%), but EPS is at its 10y high after a hard P&C/reinsurance market and consensus FY2/FY3 slows to +4.5%/+5.7%; matches the TRV/WRB peak-cycle precedent.

name: Italmobiliare S.p.A.
reason: Italian investment holding company (Pesenti family) whose EPS (EUR 2.24 in 2021, 0.37 in 2022, 1.76 in 2025) is set by portfolio disposals and fair-value marks, 10y avg ROE 4.2% and consensus FY3 -18.3%; holding-company earnings are not forecastable and not special.

name: Aviva plc
reason: UK composite insurer with adjusted EPS of GBP 0.48 (2015) to 0.56 (2025) (1.5% CAGR), 10y avg ROE 6.9%, adjusted-vs-GAAP gap of 112% and growth now from the Direct Line acquisition; restructured, ordinary returns with no organic >=7% route.

name: Cibus Real Estate AB (publ)
reason: Nordic grocery-anchored landlord with net debt/EBITDA of 11.2x, EPS losses in 2023-24 on property write-downs, FFO/share of EUR 0.95 in 2025 below the 1.02 consensus, and consensus EPS growth of +1.7%/+2.4% for FY2/FY3; levered, low-growth property income with no specialness.

name: Greencoat UK Wind Plc
reason: Listed wind-farm fund whose earnings are set by UK power prices, wind yields and NAV revaluations: EPS GBP 0.41 (2022) to -0.09 (2025) with share count up 16.9%/yr; commodity-driven and not a compounding business.

name: ENGIE S.A.
reason: French-state-controlled energy group whose EPS (EUR 0.58 in 2020, 2.20 in 2023, 1.51 in 2025) follows power and gas prices and regulated Belgian nuclear outcomes, 10y avg ROE 3.7%, EBIT margin at the 91st pctile and consensus FY2/FY3 +2.7%/+4.4%.

name: PKO Bank Polski SA
reason: Poland's dominant state-controlled bank (EPS PLN 2.22 to 9.17, 15.2% 10y CAGR) but earnings are at a NIM-driven 10y high and subject to government policy (bank tax, 2022 mortgage credit holidays, CHF-mortgage litigation costs), with consensus FY1 -3.1% and LTG 2.5%.

name: Italgas SpA
reason: Regulated Italian gas distributor whose EPS rise to EUR 0.67 (2025) leans on the 2i Rete Gas acquisition (acq/FCF 7.2x) and leverage (net debt/EBITDA 5.8x), with ARERA-set returns and long-run gas-network transition risk; regulated returns with acquisition-led growth.
